name: How can you tell if a custom home builder is underbidding your project?

mainEntity.name: How can you tell if a custom home builder is underbidding your project in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: How can you tell if a custom home builder is underbidding your project in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A custom home builder may be underbidding your project if the price is much lower than comparable bids but the proposal is vague or incomplete. Warning signs include missing site work, weak allowances, no clear permit responsibility, unrealistic schedule promises, and broad exclusions that shift major costs back to the homeowner. Another red flag is a bid that does not reflect the actual lot conditions, finish level, or structural complexity. In Los Angeles, underbids often collapse later into change orders when grading, utility work, or long-lead materials are finally addressed. Homeowners should compare bids line by line, not just by total price, and ask what assumptions each builder made. The goal is to compare the same scope, not the cheapest headline number. A properly priced custom home proposal should feel detailed, realistic, and tied to the specific property. If a number seems too good to be true, it usually is.
acceptedAnswer.description: A builder may be underbidding if the proposal is much lower than others, contains vague allowances, skips site work, omits permits or engineering, or uses unrealistic timelines. Underbidding often leads to change orders, delays, or lower-quality substitutions later.
